vignette: Emily, a 30-year-old North American woman married to her high school sweetheart, had always been content with her life until she was subjected to unimaginable torture at the hands of strangers. The traumatic event occurred during one of her rare solo trips abroad, where she found herself in a situation that spiraled out of control within moments. The trauma involved intense emotional and physical abuse over several days, leaving Emily with profound scars-both visible and invisible. Since her return, she has experienced vivid flashbacks and an overwhelming sense of fear triggered by seemingly benign situations. Emily now works as a bank teller in a small branch in downtown Chicago. Her daily routine is filled with interactions that can trigger memories of the ordeal. The expressions of anger from customers, even when they are calm and frustrated, send her into a state of heightened alertness. This has led to several uncomfortable moments where she freezes or feels compelled to leave the scene abruptly. Her fears are not limited to angry expressions; feeling watched by others also evokes intense anxiety. In the bank, she often senses that colleagues or customers are observing her more than necessary, leading her to avoid eye contact altogether. This behavior has strained her relationships with coworkers who perceive her as distant and unapproachable. Sexual situations and intimacy have become particularly distressing for Emily. Simple touches from her husband can bring back vivid memories of the trauma, making it difficult for them to maintain a physical relationship. These episodes often leave her feeling overwhelmed by emotion, causing her to retreat emotionally and physically. In an attempt to cope with these overwhelming feelings, Emily has developed several maladaptive strategies. She frequently spends hours overanalyzing the details of what happened, trying to make sense of the events that still feel surreal despite their reality. This rumination often leaves her feeling drained and exhausted. Emily's compulsive spending is another way she copes. Impulsively buying things online or at local stores provides a fleeting distraction from her intrusive thoughts and memories. While this behavior offers temporary relief, it has led to mounting financial stress and guilt. The constant state of vigilance has also affected Emily's sleep patterns. She wakes frequently during the night to check whether she is safe, unable to fully relax even in familiar environments. The unusual silence that breaks the typical nighttime sounds can trigger a sudden jolt of fear, leaving her feeling on edge until morning. Her startle response is another persistent symptom. Any unexpected noise or movement causes her to jump and feel jumpy for hours afterward. This heightened sensitivity has made it difficult for her to engage in activities she once enjoyed without being constantly aware of potential threats. Emily's memories are particularly traumatic; when they return, the emotions associated with them are so overwhelming that she often needs to pause whatever she is doing to cope. These memories come back fully relived across all senses, making it feel as though she is experiencing the trauma again in real time. Triggers can appear unexpectedly, turning ordinary moments into intense and distressing experiences. What frightened Emily most was the unpredictability of these triggers and her inability to control them. She had come to believe that a return to normalcy would never be possible without some form of help. Her marriage has suffered due to her withdrawal from intimacy, and her job performance is affected by her constant need to avoid eye contact and manage sudden emotional surges. Emily's decision to seek therapy was fueled by the realization that she could no longer bear the burden alone. She hopes that through treatment, she can regain some sense of control over her life and find a way to rebuild her relationships and work environment without the constant fear of being triggered or overwhelmed by memories. In the present moment, Emily is most afraid of reliving those traumatic experiences again, but at the same time, she harbors a deep hope that therapy will provide her with the tools to manage these overwhelming feelings and eventually lead a more peaceful life.
